commits.author: himanshk96
commits.message:
[datakit] Aggregate large-cluster count files in one group_by (#10073)

`plan_large_clusters` merged the per-task count files by running a
concat and
`group_by` on the growing merged table once per file, which is quadratic
in the
number of count files. It now reads every count table, concatenates them
once
and runs a single `group_by("dup_cluster_id").aggregate([("n",
"sum")])`. The
per-file nullable cast is dropped: the count files and the empty seed
table
share `_COUNT_SCHEMA`, and the nullable `n` only appears after the one
aggregation.

All count tables are held in driver memory at once. They are one row per
distinct sampled cluster per task, so this stays small and driver-side.

Output is unchanged. A differential harness against main compared
`plan_large_clusters` and `large_clusters_step` outputs on 300 synthetic
count
files, all identical, and StepSpec hashes do not move. The existing
large-cluster and cluster-text tests pass unchanged.

Driver-only aggregation, 3,000 rows per file drawn from 20k ids:

| count files | before | after | speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 300 | 0.57 s | 0.12 s | 5.0x |
| 3,000 | 6.25 s | 1.05 s | 6.0x |
| 400 x 50k rows | 117.1 s | 2.2 s | 52.9x |

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

[inference] Refresh Snowball GPU scores after rounding fixes (#10069)

Refresh the saved native GPU scores for the June 67B-A2B Snowball
checkpoint at step 42150. The reference file records the source, inputs
and runtime.

The old scores predate #8978, which added four compiler barriers so
inference and training round intermediate results the same way. Removing
only those barriers on the same eight H100s and runtime restores all 64
old score sets exactly. With the barriers, three cases select a
different next token.

Independent checks against FP64 formulas pass: normalization differs by
at most one BF16 rounding step, and router weights match exactly after
rounding. Existing inference-versus-training regressions also pass.
Model quality was not measured.

All 64 cases match the new reference exactly on two separate eight-H100
nodes at `bce2d5c331` and in the #9400 integration at `1c72f85f22`. See
[qualification
details](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9400#issuecomment-6133449648)
for jobs and revisions.

Follow-up to #9400, which still needs TPU and final serving backend
qualification.

Co-authored-by: Romain Yon <1596570+yonromai@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.message:
[iris] Keep preferred constraints optional during demand routing (#10065)

Keep preferred constraints optional through the autoscaler's final group
eligibility check. When a preferred region matched no group, demand
stayed unrouted even though groups satisfied every required constraint.
This restores the filtering and ranking behavior introduced in #3917.

A regression covers matching and unavailable preferred regions. All
1,976 affected safe tests passed.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[rl-data] Fix curation ingestion and retain run evidence (#10055)

Run the existing curation pipelines against local primary and auxiliary
inputs in QUICK, SAMPLE and FULL modes. Local input hashes identify
cached artifacts; changes before or during execution fail the artifact.
Use the host user for bubblewrap setup and guest ownership for image
staging. Missing candidate modules declared by the task's grading spec
can score zero; grader dependency failures and interrupts remain
unscored or incomplete. Reject demonstrated malformed source contracts
while retaining reference control thresholds.

Normalize shared Nemotron JSONL downloads once through Zephyr using its
JSONL reader, shuffle and Parquet writer. Assign original row IDs before
grouping records by component. Write one Parquet file per component,
keeping its row groups separate. Local overrides read their supplied
records directly. Bound conversion ranges and output partitions by
population size. Preparation of a 367-record, 10.5 MB cached panel
across 28 components takes 0.63 seconds including worker setup and
shutdown.

Use Docker's native image cache for Docker and gVisor. Registry sources
pull only missing images; Dockerfile sources build directly in the
daemon. Keep Skopeo for QEMU's OCI filesystem preparation and resolve it
through `PATH`. Export built images with gzip layers, including
inherited layers. Batch resource uploads and use Iris's executable node
cache for managed Python environments. The image-runtime diagnosis is
recorded in [Echo](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/705).

Append campaign invocations, source statistics and phase timings to a
FineStore catalog of curation runs beside the output report. Retain
stable Atlas IDs, admission and verification outcomes, output pointers,
and exact evidence snapshots. Failed source attempts do not inherit old
manifest counts; partial evidence remains inspectable with parse errors.
Cached artifacts retain their original attempt timing. The catalog
inherits the output directory's retention policy. Atlas can import run
statistics and output pointers from the catalog while preserving saved
reviews and difficulty measurements; that import is future work.

The reconciled full-run baseline accounts for 5,115,365 records across
146 runnable source pipelines with zero unprocessed records. Five
sources retain inconclusive verification and two are blocked from
admission by failed controls. The DAPO math dataset accounts for most
rejections: 1,772,909 exact duplicates and 1,400 conflicting-reference
rows. Counts are per recipe and can include overlapping populations.

---------

commits.message:
[inference] Align GPU refreshes with releases built from main (#9746)

Align Marin's GPU refresh instructions with releases built from reviewed
vLLM main. The fork builds, tests, and publishes wheels first. A
developer or
agent then runs Snowball's comparison of token probabilities with stored
references and opens one adoption PR. Link this procedure and its
automatic
and manual test table from root agent instructions and the weekly
refresh
workflow.

Render the descriptor and generated dependencies before replacing
gpu.toml,
so rendering failures preserve existing pins. For upstream refreshes,
replay
patches from fetched fork main; Marin's wheel pin can lag source patches
already reviewed and merged there. This PR leaves production pins
unchanged.

Supersedes #9397's staged-pin and later-promotion proposal. The
companion
workflow in marin-community/vllm#85 replaces marin-community/vllm#76.
All 9
affected tests and the strict docs build pass. The developer or agent
preparing
each wheel adoption runs the live Snowball test.

Part of #9300

dispatch one from main, raise the consumer's minimum when the feature

merges.

commits.message:
[inference] Keep Snowball serving axes on mesh (#9401)

## Summary

Keep size-one `expert` and `context` axes on Levanter's inference mesh.
Snowball's explicit partition specs name these axes even on a
single-axis serving slice. Without them, the first forward pass fails
with `Resource axis: expert ... is not found in mesh` after the 67B
export loads.

## Validation

- `tests/inference/test_serve.py -k inference_mesh`: 3 passed.
- Project changed-file lint and type checks passed.
- The June Snowball 67B exported-checkpoint H100 parity cell passed all
64 representative prompts with this exact patch applied in #9400's
then-head `8f6f28c63c`; maximum probability error was 0.056754 against
the existing 0.075 bound.

This small backend fix is the base for the focused TPU parity PR #9400.
It does not change the checkpoint, prompts, or numerical bounds.

Co-authored-by: Romain Yon <1596570+yonromai@users.noreply.github.com>
